mainTopic: Dozing versus deep sleep at the פסח meal, the חצות deadline for the פסח and מצה, and the decree that פיגול and נותר make the hands טמא
overview: This amud finishes the last משנה of מסכת פסחים and its גמרא. רבי יוסי rules that someone who only dozed during the פסח meal may keep eating, but someone who fell into a deep sleep may not. רב אשי defines dozing as being half-asleep, and a story about אביי and רבה shows the rule in practice. The משנה also says that the פסח after חצות makes the hands טמא, which implies that it becomes נותר at חצות. רב יוסף explains that this follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who learns a חצות deadline from 'בלילה הזה' by comparing it to the night of מכת בכורות. רבי עקיבא disagrees and allows eating until dawn because of 'חפזון', and the two תנאים explain the words 'בלילה', 'הזה' and 'בקר' according to their views. רבא adds that for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, מצה nowadays also must be eaten before חצות. Finally, רב הונא and רב חסדא disagree about why the חכמים decreed that פיגול and נותר make the hands טמא, and about the minimum amount needed.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: Dozing Versus Deep Sleep at the פסח Meal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי rules that people who dozed may continue eating the פסח, but people who fell fast asleep may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: If they dozed, they may eat. If they fell fast asleep, they may not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings רבי יוסי's ruling about people who fall asleep in the middle of eating the קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קרבן פסח must be eaten in one continuous sitting. A deep sleep breaks that sitting, as if the person left the meal, so he may not go back and eat more. Light dozing does not break the sitting, so he may continue.

keyTerms.meaning: they dozed, they slept lightly
they fell into a deep sleep
they may eat

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice that someone who fell deeply asleep before finishing the אפיקומן should not eat it afterward. Light dozing is not a problem.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
if they dozed, they may eat;
if they fell fast asleep, they may not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's discussion of people who fell asleep during the פסח meal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dozing does not interrupt eating the פסח. Deep sleep does interrupt it, and the person may no longer eat.

steps.title: The פסח After חצות Makes the Hands טמא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the פסח after חצות makes the hands טמא, because פיגול and נותר make the hands טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסח after חצות makes the hands טמא. פיגול and נותר make the hands טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new rule: after חצות, leftover meat of the פסח makes a person's hands טמא. It explains that this is because פיגול and נותר both have this power.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים made a decree that touching פיגול or נותר makes the hands טמא. This was meant to keep the כהנים careful with sacrificial meat. Once the time for eating the פסח passes at חצות, the leftover meat counts as נותר, so it falls under this decree.

keyTerms.meaning: midnight
makes the hands ritually impure
a קרבן ruined by a wrong intention during its offering
sacrificial meat left over after its time for eating has passed

phrases.english: The Paschal lamb after midnight
makes the hands impure.
Piggul and notar
make the hands impure.
phrases.notes: This explains why the פסח after midnight has this status.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַפֶּסַח אַחַר חֲצוֹת מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַיָּדַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new halacha in the משנה about the time limit for eating the פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After חצות the פסח counts as נותר and makes the hands טמא, just like פיגול and נותר.

steps.title: What Counts as Dozing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יוסי and asks how to define 'dozing'.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי יוסי says: If they dozed, they may eat; if they fell fast asleep, they may not eat. What is the case of dozing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting רבי יוסי's words. It then asks exactly what kind of sleep counts as 'dozing'. This question sets up רב אשי's definition in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the halacha depends on the difference between dozing and deep sleep, we need a clear line between them. The גמרא asks for that definition.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the case? how does it look?
one who dozed

phrases.english: Gemara:
Rabbi Yosei says: if they dozed, they may eat;
if they fell fast asleep, they may not eat.
What is the case of dozing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יוסי's ruling from step 1 and asks for a definition of its key term.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact definition of נתנמנם (dozing), as opposed to deep sleep.

steps.title: רב אשי Defines Dozing
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that dozing is a half-asleep state: the person answers when called but cannot answer sensibly, and he remembers once he is reminded.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Asleep but not asleep, awake but not awake. For example, when people call him he answers, but he cannot give a sensible reply, and when they remind him, he remembers.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question by describing the in-between state of dozing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three signs of dozing. He responds when called. He cannot give a reasoned answer. He remembers what happened once reminded. Deep sleep would mean he does not respond at all.

keyTerms.meaning: asleep but not asleep
awake but not awake
to give back a sensible answer
he remembers

steps.confusionAlert: Answering when called does NOT mean he is fully awake. He is still only 'dozing' if he cannot give a sensible reply. Being reminded and remembering is part of the same definition, not a separate test.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
asleep but not asleep,
awake but not awake.
For example, when they call him, he answers,
but he does not know how to give a sensible reply,
and when they remind him, he remembers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dozing is a half-asleep state: he responds when called but not sensibly, and he remembers when reminded.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical test for whether someone at the סדר may still eat after drifting off.

steps.title: אביי Sees רבה Nodding Off
steps.stepSummary: אביי sees רבה dozing at the meal and asks him whether he is sleeping.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי was sitting before רבה. He saw that רבה was dozing. He said to him: Is the Master sleeping?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story: אביי notices his רבי, רבה, nodding off and asks if he is asleep. This sets up רבה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's question carries a halachic concern. If רבה were truly asleep, he would no longer be allowed to keep eating.

keyTerms.meaning: was sitting before him (as a student)
is the Master really sleeping?

phrases.english: Abaye was sitting before Rabba.
He saw that he was dozing,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מֵינָם קָא נָאֵים מָר.
phrases.english: he said to him: Is the Master sleeping?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life story that applies the dozing rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבה is truly asleep, which would stop him from continuing to eat.

steps.title: רבה: I Am Only Dozing, So I May Eat
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that he is only dozing and quotes the משנה that people who doze may still eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am only dozing, and we learned: If they dozed, they may eat; if they fell fast asleep, they may not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי that he is only dozing, not truly asleep. He supports this with רבי יוסי's ruling in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story shows that dozing does not stop someone from eating. It also shows that the אמוראים followed רבי יוסי's view in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: I am only dozing

steps.whatToRemember: Light dozing (half-asleep, answers when called, remembers later) does not break the פסח meal. Deep sleep does. The halacha follows רבי יוסי, as shown by רבה's conduct.

phrases.english: He said to him: I am only dozing,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and we learned: if they dozed, they may eat;
if they fell fast asleep, they may not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question from step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבה was only dozing, and by the משנה a dozer may continue eating.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוסי's rule is applied in practice.

steps.title: Inference: The פסח Becomes נותר at חצות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the second part of the משנה and infers that from חצות on, the פסח counts as נותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסח after חצות makes the hands טמא, etc. Apparently, from חצות it is considered נותר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second rule in the משנה. It draws a conclusion from it: the eating time of the פסח ends at חצות, and after that the meat is נותר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה links the פסח after midnight to פיגול and נותר. That link implies that its time limit ends at חצות and not at dawn. The גמרא points out this implication so it can ask who holds it.

keyTerms.meaning: apparently, it follows that
it becomes, it is considered

steps.confusionAlert: Not everyone agrees that the eating time of the פסח ends at חצות. Some hold it can be eaten until dawn. That is exactly why the גמרא will ask who holds this view.

phrases.aramaic: הַפֶּסַח אַחַר חֲצוֹת מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַיָּדַיִם וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: The Paschal lamb after midnight makes the hands impure, etc.
Apparently, from midnight
it is considered notar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the second rule of the משנה (step 2).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the משנה, the time for eating the פסח ends at חצות, after which it is נותר.

steps.title: Who Is the תנא Behind This View?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that the פסח may only be eaten until חצות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא's opinion this משנה follows. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a disagreement among the תנאים about how late the פסח may be eaten. The גמרא wants to know whose side of that disagreement our משנה takes.

keyTerms.meaning: who is the תנא (whose view is this)?

phrases.english: Who is the tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the inference in step 7 and asks for its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who holds that the פסח becomes נותר at חצות.

steps.title: רב יוסף Names the תנא: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that the תנא who limits the פסח to חצות is רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: It is רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 8. רב יוסף identifies the משנה's view as the view of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה implied that after חצות the פסח is already נותר. That is not everyone's opinion, so the גמרא needed a name. רב יוסף gives it, and the next step brings the ברייתא that proves it.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
It is Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The view of the משנה belongs to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: The ברייתא: Learning חצות from the Night of מכת בכורות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה uses a גזירה שוה to limit eating the פסח to חצות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: 'And they shall eat the meat on this night.' רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: Here it says 'on this night,' and later it says 'And I will pass through the land of Egypt on this night.' Just as there it means until חצות, so too here it means until חצות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף proves his answer with a ברייתא. In it, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה links two פסוקים that share the words 'בלילה הזה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about eating the פסח does not say when the night ends. The פסוק about מכת בכורות uses the same words, and that event happened at חצות. So the time limit for eating the פסח is also חצות.

keyTerms.meaning: It says here ... and it says there: the formula of a גזירה שוה
Just as there ... so too here
Midnight
And I will pass through (said of מכת בכורות)

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'until midnight' is not written in the פסוק of 'ועברתי' itself. It comes from the earlier פסוק 'כחצות הלילה אני יוצא', which describes the same night of מכת בכורות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the view that the מצוה of eating the פסח, and in practice the אפיקומן, ends at חצות.

phrases.english: As it was taught: 'And they shall eat the meat on this night,'
Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
It is stated here 'on this night,'
and it is stated below
'And I will pass through the land of Egypt on this night.'
Just as below, it is until midnight,
so too here, it is until midnight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that backs רב יוסף's identification.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר בן עזריה holds the פסח may be eaten only until חצות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא using a גזירה שוה between שמות יב:ח and שמות יב:יב.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the word 'haste' means until dawn
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא objects. The word 'חפזון' shows that the פסח may be eaten until the time of haste, which is dawn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: But it already says 'in haste.' That means until the time of haste.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, רבי עקיבא challenges רבי אלעזר בן עזריה with a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says the פסח is eaten 'בחפזון', in haste. The great rush happened at dawn, when the Jews left מצרים. So for רבי עקיבא the time limit is dawn, not חצות.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it already stated? (introduces a challenge)
Haste
The time of haste, meaning dawn

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:
But wasn't 'haste' already stated?
It means until the time of haste.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: וַהֲלֹא נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the time limit derived in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's derivation that the time limit is חצות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different פסוק ('חפזון') points to a later time limit, dawn.

steps.title: Then why does the verse say 'at night'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא raises a question against his own view: if the limit comes from 'חפזון', what does the word 'בלילה' teach?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does the verse come to teach by saying 'at night'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא raises a question against himself. This sets up his explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'חפזון' sets the time limit at dawn, the word 'בלילה' seems extra. So רבי עקיבא must show that it teaches some other rule.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
What does the verse come to teach?

phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach by saying 'at night'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the word 'בלילה' teaches if רבי עקיבא's reading in Step 11 is right.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word 'בלילה' teaches according to רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: 'At night' teaches that the פסח is not eaten by day
steps.stepSummary: The word 'בלילה' teaches that, unlike other קדשים, the פסח is eaten only at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the פסח is eaten during the day, like other offerings. So the verse says 'at night': it is eaten at night, and it is not eaten during the day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers his own question. 'בלילה' tells us when the eating happens, not when it must end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most קדשים are eaten by day. Without this word, we might have thought the פסח could be eaten by day too. So רבי עקיבא uses 'בלילה' for this teaching, and the end time comes from 'חפזון'.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought
Sacrificial offerings
Therefore the verse says

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: the פסח may be eaten only until חצות, learned from מכת בכורות. רבי עקיבא: it may be eaten until dawn, learned from 'חפזון'. The משנה, which treats the פסח as נותר after חצות, follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

phrases.english: One might think it is eaten like other offerings, by day.
Therefore the verse says: 'at night,'
at night it is eaten,
and it is not eaten by day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 12 by giving 'בלילה' a different teaching.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'בלילה' excludes eating the פסח by day, the way other קדשים are eaten.

steps.title: What does רבי עקיבא learn from the word 'that'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי עקיבא does with the word 'הזה', since he does not use it for the גזירה שוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא, what does he do with this word 'הזה' ('that')?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה used 'הזה' for his גזירה שוה, so what does רבי עקיבא, who rejects that גזירה שוה, learn from it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah does not waste words. Since רבי עקיבא does not use 'הזה' to limit the פסח to חצות, it must teach him something else. This sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That', from 'בַּלַּיְלָה הַזֶּה', the word used in the גזירה שוה
What does he do with it? (What does he learn from it?)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva, this word 'that'
phrases.notes: This is the word 'that' from 'on that night' in the פסוק (שמות יב:ח).

phrases.english: what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, הַאי ״הַזֶּה״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier pattern. After asking what 'בלילה' teaches, the גמרא now asks what 'הזה' teaches for רבי עקיבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra rule רבי עקיבא learns from the word 'הזה'

steps.title: The word 'that' excludes a second night
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא uses 'הזה' to teach that the פסח may not be eaten on a second night, even though one might have compared it to שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it to exclude another night. Otherwise you might think: the פסח is קדשים קלים and שלמים are קדשים קלים. Just as שלמים are eaten for two days and one night, so too the פסח. We would just swap nights for days, so the פסח would be eaten for two nights and one day. So the Torah wrote 'הזה': only that one night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for רבי עקיבא, 'הזה' teaches that the פסח is eaten on that one night only, not a second night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without 'הזה' we might compare the פסח to שלמים, which belong to the same category of קדשים קלים and are eaten for two days and the night between. Since the פסח starts at night, we would flip it to two nights and the day between. 'הזה' blocks that comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude
You might have thought (introduces a mistaken assumption)
Offerings of lesser holiness
Peace-offerings, eaten for two days and one night
I will put nights in place of days

steps.confusionAlert: Being קדשים קלים is still true of the פסח. The comparison only fails on the length of eating time. 'הזה' makes the פסח's eating period a one-night exception within its category.

phrases.english: He needs it to exclude
it comes to exclude another night.
It could enter your mind to say:
since the Paschal lamb is an offering of lesser holiness,
and peace-offerings are offerings of lesser holiness,
just as peace-offerings are eaten

phrases.aramaic: לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אֶחָד, אַף פֶּסַח;
phrases.english: for two days and one night, so too the Paschal lamb;
I will put nights in place of days,

phrases.aramaic: וִיהֵא נֶאֱכָל לִשְׁנֵי לֵילוֹת וְיוֹם אֶחָד,
phrases.english: so it will be eaten for two nights and one day.
Therefore the Torah wrote: 'that'.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְמַעוֹטֵי לַיְלָה אַחֵר הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'הזה' excludes a second night, which we might otherwise have learned by comparing the פסח to שלמים.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learns 'one night' from 'do not leave over until morning'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה does not need 'הזה' to exclude a second night, because 'לא תותירו עד בקר' already teaches it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר בן עזריה would tell you: this is learned from 'You shall not leave any of it over until morning'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, who used 'הזה' for his גזירה שוה, still knows the פסח is not eaten on a second night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an unspoken question: if 'הזה' is busy with the גזירה שוה, where does רבי אלעזר בן עזריה get the one-night rule? He answers that if nothing may be left until morning, it certainly cannot be eaten the next night.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you (a reply given on someone's behalf)
Do not leave any of it over until morning (שמות יב:י)
It is derived

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אָמַר לָךְ:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya would say to you:

phrases.aramaic: מִ״לֹּא תוֹתִירוּ עַד בֹּקֶר״ נָפְקָא הָא.
phrases.english: this is derived from 'You shall not leave over until morning'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אָמַר לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the other תנא has a different source for the same rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי אלעזר בן עזריה uses 'הזה' for the גזירה שוה, he would have no source excluding a second night.
steps.terutzMaskana: He learns it from 'לא תותירו עד בקר'.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: 'morning' alone could mean the second morning
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that 'לא תותירו עד בקר' is not enough by itself, since 'בקר' could be read as the second morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא would tell you: if the Torah had not written 'הזה', I would have said that 'בקר' means the second morning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא pushes back. He argues that 'לא תותירו עד בקר' alone does not prove the one-night rule, so 'הזה' is still needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'בקר' could mean the morning after the second night, the verse would match the two-nights idea from שלמים. So for רבי עקיבא, only 'הזה' firmly limits eating to the first night.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (a possible but rejected understanding)
The second morning

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva would say to you:
If the Torah had not written 'that',
I would have said:
what is 'morning'? The second morning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the alternative source offered in Step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Whether 'לא תותירו עד בקר' alone proves the פסח is eaten on one night only
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'בקר' is unclear and could mean the second morning.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: 'morning' always means the first morning
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that whenever the Torah writes 'בקר', it means the very next morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר would tell you: wherever the Torah writes 'בקר', it means the first morning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר defends his source. 'בקר' always means the next morning, so 'לא תותירו עד בקר' is enough, and 'הזה' is free for his גזירה שוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disagreement comes down to how to read 'בקר'. For רבי אלעזר, its plain meaning is the next morning, so no second night is possible. The sugya ends with each תנא holding his own reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Anywhere that it is written
The first (next) morning

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים agree the פסח is eaten on one night only. They argue about the source. רבי עקיבא learns it from 'הזה'. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה learns it from 'לא תותירו עד בקר' and uses 'הזה' for the חצות גזירה שוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the two opinions on חצות versus dawn each account for every word in the פסוקים without contradiction.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar would say to you:
Anywhere that 'morning' is written,
it means the first morning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי עקיבא's rejection in Step 17.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בקר' in the Torah always means the first morning, so 'לא תותירו' alone excludes a second night.

steps.title: רבא: מצה eaten after חצות nowadays does not count, according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that, according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, someone who eats מצה after חצות in our times, when there is no קרבן פסח, has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If a person ate מצה nowadays after חצות, then according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה he has not fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא applies רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's חצות deadline for the פסח to the מצוה of eating מצה nowadays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the previous steps, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה held that the פסח may only be eaten until חצות. רבא says the same deadline applies to מצה, even today when there is no פסח at all. So under this view, מצה eaten after חצות does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Nowadays, when there is no בית המקדש and no קרבן פסח
Midnight
He has not fulfilled his obligation
Unleavened bread eaten on the first night of פסח

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the source of the common practice of trying to eat the אפיקומן before חצות, to satisfy רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view as well.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אָכַל מַצָּה בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה אַחַר חֲצוֹת,
phrases.english: If one ate matza nowadays after midnight,
according to Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
phrases.notes: He is the one who holds the פסח may only be eaten until midnight.

phrases.english: he has not fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אָכַל מַצָּה בִּזְמַן הַזֶּה אַחַר חֲצוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's חצות deadline for the פסח (steps 9–10) and applies it to the eating of מצה today.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, מצה eaten after חצות nowadays does not fulfill the obligation.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious, since מצה is linked to the קרבן פסח?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: his ruling seems obvious, because the Torah links מצה to the פסח, so מצה should naturally follow the פסח's time limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is obvious! Since מצה is linked by the verse to the קרבן פסח, it is treated just like the קרבן פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבא needed to say this at all, since the answer seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'על מצות ומררים יאכלהו' places מצה together with the פסח, which creates a היקש (a link that makes them share laws). If they share laws, then the פסח's חצות deadline should automatically apply to מצה. So what new point is רבא teaching?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge that a statement teaches nothing new)
It was linked by a היקש, a comparison the Torah makes by placing two things together
It is similar to / treated like

phrases.english: It is obvious!
For since it is juxtaposed to the Pesach offering,
phrases.notes: From the פסוק 'על מצות ומררים יאכלהו': they eat the פסח together with מצה.

phrases.english: it is considered like the Pesach offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבא's ruling adds anything new.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The היקש between מצה and the פסח already makes מצה follow the פסח's time limit, so רבא's ruling seems obvious.

steps.title: The verse took מצה out of the link, but then put it back
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: one might think a separate פסוק cut מצה off from the היקש. רבא teaches that the repeated פסוק returns מצה to its original status, so it keeps the פסח's rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: the verse took מצה out of the היקש. So רבא teaches us that when the verse repeated it, it brought it back to its original status.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא's ruling is not obvious. There was a real reason to think the היקש no longer applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that 'בערב תאכלו מצות' makes מצה its own obligation, even with no פסח. That could suggest the Torah removed מצה from the היקש entirely, so it would have no חצות limit. רבא teaches that this repetition only keeps the מצוה alive nowadays, and it brings מצה back to its original rules, including the חצות deadline.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
The verse took it out of the היקש
It teaches us (the new point being made)
It brought it back / repeated it
The original matter, its first status

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, מצה nowadays has the same חצות deadline as the פסח. The Torah's separate command to eat מצה keeps the מצוה alive without the פסח, but it does not cancel the shared time limit.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the Torah's separate command 'בערב תאכלו מצות' frees מצה from all of the פסח's rules. It only makes מצה an obligation on its own. The time limit from the היקש still applies.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
The verse has removed it from the juxtaposition.
phrases.notes: The פסוק here is 'בערב תאכלו מצות', which makes eating מצה a מצוה all on its own.

phrases.english: So he teaches us
that when the verse repeated it,
it restored it to its original status.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הָא אַפְּקֵיהּ קְרָא מֵהֶיקֵּישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge by showing there was a reason to think otherwise.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows there was a plausible mistaken assumption that the statement corrects
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a separate פסוק makes מצה obligatory without the פסח, מצה has been removed from the היקש and has no חצות limit.
steps.terutzMaskana: The repeated פסוק returns מצה to its original status, so it still follows the פסח's חצות deadline.

steps.title: Why the חכמים decreed that פיגול and נותר make the hands טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that פיגול and נותר make the hands טמא. רב הונא and רב חסדא disagree about the reason: one says it is because of suspected כהנים, the other because of lazy כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: פיגול and נותר make the hands טמא, etc. רב הונא and רב חסדא disagree. One said: because of suspected כהנים. The other said: because of lazy כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new line in the משנה and brings a disagreement about why the חכמים made this rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Touching פיגול or נותר does not make the hands טמא by Torah law. This is a rabbinic decree. One view says it targets כהנים suspected of deliberately making קרבנות into פיגול, so the decree discourages them. The other view says it targets lazy כהנים who let the meat become נותר, so the decree pushes them to eat it on time.

keyTerms.meaning: A קרבן made invalid by an improper intention about the time for eating or offering it
Meat of a קרבן left over past its time for eating
Makes the hands ritually impure
כהנים suspected of deliberately invalidating קרבנות
Lazy כהנים who let the meat become נותר

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not tell us which of the two אמוראים holds which view. It just says 'one said' and 'the other said'.

phrases.aramaic: הַפִּיגּוּל וְהַנּוֹתָר מְטַמֵּא אֶת הַיָּדַיִם וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Piggul and notar render the hands impure, etc.
phrases.notes: A quotation from the משנה, opening the new topic.

phrases.english: Rav Huna and Rav Chisda disagree:
one said: because of suspected priests,
and one said: because of lazy priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the last clause of the משנה (step 2), the decree that פיגול and נותר make the hands טמא. That decree is the reason the פסח after חצות makes the hands טמא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The decree that פיגול and נותר make the hands טמא was made either because of suspected כהנים or because of lazy כהנים.

steps.title: How much פיגול or נותר is needed to make the hands טמא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא and רב חסדא also disagree about the minimum amount: one says a כזית, the other says a כביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One said: a כזית (olive-bulk). And one said: a כביצה (egg-bulk).
steps.whatsHappening: The same two אמוראים have a second disagreement, this time about how much meat is needed for the decree to apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כזית is the smaller amount, so that view applies the decree more widely. A כביצה is the larger amount, the usual measure for food טומאה, so that view applies it more narrowly. The two disagreements are listed side by side, which sets up the possibility that they are connected.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-bulk (the smaller measure)
An egg-bulk (the larger measure, standard for food טומאה)
One of them said

phrases.english: One said: an olive-bulk,
and one said: an egg-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד אָמַר: כְּזַיִת, וְחַד אָמַר: כְּבֵיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second disagreement between the same two אמוראים about the same decree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute whether a כזית or a כביצה of פיגול or נותר is needed to make the hands טמא.
